title: ChatBurst spiral bench driver to detect p95 token-regressions under bursty streaming load
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a novel load driver (ChatBurst Spiral) that generates bursty, spiraling concurrency patterns for SSE and WebSocket streaming chat/completions to exercise realistic token-per-second dynamics, KV-cache hit/miss transitions, and p95 latency regressions across multi-tenant deployments. This ticket covers the prototype harness, integration into CI regression gates, and a dashboard/reporting pipeline for automated alerting when tokenflow p95 or tokens/sec trends regress beyond configured baselines.
acceptance_criteria: Driver can run SSE and WebSocket scenarios with parameterized burst windows, spiral ramp-up/down, and per-tenant token curves
Recorded metrics include tokens/sec (global and per-tenant), p50/p95/p99 latencies for token emission, connection churn, and backend KV-cache hit-rate
Automated regression detection with historical baseline comparison is wired into CI: new builds fail when p95 increases by >15% sustained over N runs or tokens/sec drops by >20%
Grafana dashboard with annotated runs, artifacts persisted to S3, and a reproducible driver runbook available in Confluence
Prototype validated on dedicated-small cluster (synthetic tenants=50, avg session length=800 tokens) with measured baseline report in the ticket comments
approach: Implement a lightweight Go-based client harness that can multiplex virtual sessions over a pool of TCP connections to emulate connection re-use and realistic SSE/WSS framing
Support configurable user profiles: short-chat (10-100 tokens), medium-chat (200-800 tokens), long-chat (1k-4k tokens) with per-profile KV-cache priming delays
Introduce 'spiral' load pattern: repeated short bursts increasing concurrency by 10% each step for 12 steps, then gentle decay, to expose transient scheduling and kernel-selection regressions
Instrument harness to emit structured JSON telemetry to a local aggregator which forwards to Grafana/Prometheus and S3-run artifacts for offline analysis
Add a regression detector service (python) that compares latest run histograms to rolling baseline using KS-test + relative heuristics and opens a GitHub issue when thresholds exceeded
test_plan: Unit tests for protocol encoding/decoding and multiplexing layer (CI run)
Smoke run on dev cluster (sustained 1k tokens/sec) to validate connection stability and telemetry correctness
Scale test in staging with 50 tenants x simulated 200 concurrent sessions for 1 hour to gather p95 baselines
A/B regression runs: compare new runtime/quantization kernel to baseline across identical spiral sequences and validate automatic detector behavior
Chaos injection: add 5% random request failures and 10% KV-cache cold miss rate to ensure harness reproduces real-world tail effects
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed — PoC client multiplexing works locally (small Go binary). Notes: multiplexing reduces per-connection overhead and reveals per-client KV cache behavior earlier.
2026-02-18: Design review with Eng + Perf team. Decided on spiral pattern parameters (12 steps, 10% step growth, 30s per step). Action: add config YAML and seedable RNG for reproducibility.
2026-02-24: Implemented telemetry emitter and local aggregator. Added Prometheus metrics: tokens_total, tokens_per_sec, token_emit_latency_seconds_bucket, connection_open_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio.

2026-03-02: First staging run with 50 synthetic tenants. Baseline artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/chatburst/ENG-688450/baseline-20260302.tar.gz. Observed p95 token-emit latency = 78ms, tokens/sec = 4,200 (aggregate).

2026-03-06: Created initial regression detector prototype — uses 3-run rolling baseline and flags p95 delta >15% OR tokens/sec drop >20%. Hooked to CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/8421
2026-03-10: Integrations review — Grafana panels added (run annotations, heatmap of p95 by tenant). Work remaining: improve KV priming model and add consistent artifact metadata for reproducibility.
runbook: If regression detector opens an alert, run 'benchctl compare --left baseline --right latest --metric p95 --alpha 0.05' to reproduce statistical result
For p95 regression <30%: triage with perf team; examine kernel selection logs and KV-cache hit-rate spikes
For p95 regression >=30% or tokens/sec drop >=40%: roll back runtime image and create incident (reference: INC-12456) — notify platform-sre and perf oncall
If detector false-positive suspected: replay both runs using same random seed and client profile YAML from artifact bundle and re-evaluate
Recording: preserve artifacts and run metadata in S3 with tag 'regression-<build-number>' for postmortem
notes: Tradeoffs: we intentionally bias spiral to short bursts to expose scheduling thrash; this increases cost of runs but improves sensitivity to token-emit tail effects
KV-cache priming: naive priming causes unrealistic perfect-hit warm-ups; we added configurable cold-start percentage to mimic real traffic
Cost estimate: staging suite ~8 GPU hours per full spiral run at 4k tokens/sec aggregate; aim to optimize by smarter sampling once detector is stable
Next: wire detector to Linear->Slack integration to automatically file regression tickets with artifacts attached
